paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about the end of Romans. Paul stops to name people. Phoebe, "a servant of the church in Cenchrea," who "has been a great help to many people" (Romans 16:1-2). Prisca and Aquila, who "have risked their lives" for him (Romans 16:3-4). Mary, who "has worked very hard for you" (Romans 16:6). God's work isn't carried by one famous name, it's carried by a whole crowd of people who showed up, helped and kept going.

That's why the warning lands so hard. Paul urges them to "watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned" and to turn away from them (Romans 16:17). Those people serve "their own appetites," and they use "smooth talk and flattery" on the naive (Romans 16:18). So Paul wants the believers to be "wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil" (Romans 16:19). Friend, I think the lesson is to know the teaching so well that a sweet voice can't talk you out of it.

And look at where Paul lands. He ends with praise "to the only wise God" who is able to strengthen them, and he says the mystery once hidden is now "revealed and made known" to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith (Romans 16:25-27). Paul says it all comes "through Jesus Christ." So the same God who strengthens you is the One you give the glory to, and that's worth staying ready for, just like my ovens.
